room.title: Operations Professionals
room.description: How an operations coordinator runs a warehouse cutover and a supplier onboarding push in the same week — the counts, the run-book, the compliance checks and what's still being chased, all on one surface.

desks.title: Fulfilment cutover — Riverside warehouse to the Eastgate 3PL
desks.description: Moving 79 pallets and every live order out of our own warehouse and into the 3PL: transfer counts, the go-live run-book and the barcode gap that could stall receiving.
desks.brief:
## Fulfilment cutover — Riverside to Eastgate

**Business** Larchmere Home · homewares, online and wholesale
**Go-live** orders route to the Eastgate 3PL from @+6d
**Order hold** 48 hours before go-live — nothing dispatches while the last pallets move
**Riverside lease** ends @+20d, so there is no second attempt

### What moves
- 79 pallets, 15,820 units, 10 product lines, 612 active SKUs
- Open wholesale orders and the returns stock
- Carrier pickups switch from Riverside to Eastgate's dock

### Definition of done
- Every pallet counted in at Eastgate, unit variance under 0.5%
- First 200 orders picked at 99.5% accuracy or better
- Same-day dispatch for orders in by 2pm, from day one

### Where it stands
38 of 79 pallets are counted in. Variance on those is 30 units (0.37%), inside tolerance — glassware is the exception, with 18 broken units now on a freight claim. **The real risk is 41 SKUs with no barcode**: Eastgate can't receive them until they're labelled.

callout.title: Blocking: 41 SKUs with no barcode
callout.body: Eastgate's system won't receive a SKU it can't scan. 41 SKUs, mostly gift sets and storage jars, need labels printed and applied before the storage pallets leave Riverside @+2d. Labels are the Cobalt trial order on the supplier desk.

blocks.p: One owner per step. If a step fails, stop and call the next name before moving on — orders stay held until step 6 is done.

ol: 06:00 — Rhys confirms the last pallets are counted in and the variance is logged
07:00 — Order sync switched from Riverside to Eastgate in the store admin; old pick list disabled
07:30 — Ten test orders across all three carriers; Carmen confirms they land in the 3PL queue
09:00 — Test parcels scanned out; tracking numbers reach the customer emails
10:00 — Hana publishes the 'where is my order' macro for the hold backlog
11:00 — Hold released; about 640 held orders pick in order-date sequence

blocks.p: If test orders haven't synced by 09:00, the hold extends by one day. **No orders route back to Riverside once stock has left** — Carmen and Rhys make the call together.

ul: Riverside floor and the last pallets — Rhys
Customer service macro and backlog emails — Hana
Store admin and order sync — me

notes.title: Ops stand-up — what I'm holding
notes.body:
Context I'd otherwise lose between the dock and the inbox:

- Glassware claim: photos sent to the carrier, they want the pallet labels too
- Cookware 4 short, knives 8 short — probably the returns cage; recount @+1d before raising anything
- Carmen says Eastgate's real cutoff is 1:30pm to make the 2pm promise
- Packing slips still print the Riverside returns address

Ask Eastgate: can they apply barcodes on receipt, and what does it cost per unit?

stickies.title: Today
stickies.body:
1. Barcode list to Cobalt
2. Book gift sets pickup
3. Recount cookware + knives
4. 2pm call with Carmen

stickies.title: Don't forget
stickies.body: Returns address on the website, packing slips and the auto-reply — before go-live.

desks.title: Supplier onboarding — eight vendors for the Coastal range
desks.description: Getting eight new suppliers from first email to first purchase order: documents, compliance checks, trial orders and the one test report that gates the ceramics order.
desks.brief:
## Supplier onboarding — Coastal range

**Scope** 8 new suppliers · packaging, freight, product and services
**Gate** trial orders only (under $2k) until a supplier is Approved in the finance system
**Ceramics PO** must be raised by @+9d — 10-week lead time to make the range launch

### Six documents from every supplier
- Signed supplier agreement, payment terms 30 days end of month
- Tax and business registration details
- Bank details, verified by a call-back to a number we found ourselves
- Certificate of insurance — public and product liability
- Ethical sourcing questionnaire
- Product test reports, or a site induction for on-site services

### Where it stands
33 of 48 documents are in. One supplier is approved and two are running trial orders. Estimated annual spend across all eight is $409k.

**Tidewater Ceramics is the one to watch.** Their food-contact test report is three years old and our limit is two, so the ceramics PO can't be raised until a current report arrives. At $126k a year, Tidewater is 31% of that $409k.

callout.title: Gate: Tidewater's test report
callout.body: Food-contact (lead and cadmium) test reports must be under two years old. Theirs is three. Their lab quotes 7 days for a retest — if it isn't booked by @+2d, the @+9d order date slips and the range launches without ceramics.

rows.next: Resend pack — went to a former employee
Wait for Eastgate's pallet pooling answer

blocks.h3: How a supplier gets to Approved

blocks.p: The same seven steps for every supplier, in this order. Nobody skips step 4, whoever is asking.

ol: Owner sends the onboarding pack and logs the supplier here as Docs requested
Supplier returns the six documents; owner checks each one against the brief
Finance creates the supplier record as inactive, so nothing can be paid yet
Bank details verified by phone, to a number we found independently — never one from the same email
Compliance check: insurance dates, test reports, ethical sourcing answers
Trial order under $2k, inspected on arrival at Eastgate
Ops lead approves; finance activates the record and the first PO can go out

ul: A bank detail change by email is treated as fraud until a call-back proves otherwise
Expired insurance sends a supplier back to Compliance check, even mid-order
Spend estimates are re-checked after the first quarter of real orders

blocks.quote: A supplier that's slow with documents now will be slow with stock later.

notes.title: Supplier calls — what I'm holding
notes.body:
- Bluegum emailed 'updated' bank details yesterday — call-back to the number on their website, not the one in the email
- Tidewater's lab can retest in 7 days if samples ship this week; Ngozi is pricing the courier
- Spinifex's insurance renews @+6d — ask for the new certificate, not the expiring one
- Northpoint is waiting on us, not the other way round

Decide with finance: do we accept a test report from the factory's own lab, or only from an accredited one?

stickies.title: This week
stickies.body:
Call-back to Bluegum
Book Tidewater retest
Cobalt labels @+2d
Chase Spinifex insurance

stickies.title: Fraud check
stickies.body: Any 'our bank details have changed' email: stop, and call the number we already hold.
